Subject: Evaluation timeline + surge/overage question

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team liked the latency profile and the KV caching notes. We're pulling together a six-week evaluation and a short mutual action plan so procurement can sign off. Two quick questions we need clarified before we present to legal/procurement: 

1) During the 6-week onramp (we expect a step from staging -> pilot -> production), how does Redwood price transient surges that exceed committed baseline? Is that billed at a per-token surge rate or is there a staged overage slab?

2) Are there explicit safeguards (caps or per-window throttles) we can include in the MAP so we don't get unexpected invoice spikes during synthetic load or a one-off stress test?

We can share the proposed MAP we use internally — would prefer Redwood to propose language we can include directly in the trial statement of work. Procurement will want a clear cap or notified-exceed threshold.

Attaching our internal evaluation checklist for context.

Thanks,
Samir Patel
Head of ML Platforms
Glyph Analytics

Attachment: glyph-eval-checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com

Cc: ben.carter@redwoodinference.com, laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com

Subject: Re: Evaluation timeline + surge/overage question

Hi Samir — great to meet the team yesterday. Appreciate the checklist, that's helpful context.

Short answers up front:
- We offer two mechanisms for transient overage during an evaluation onramp: a short-term surge rate (per-token) and an alternative staged-slab pricing for sustained bursts that exceed the committed baseline for more than 24 hours.
- We can include a protective cap in the MAP (example language below) that prevents billing above an agreed monthly overage threshold without explicit written approval from Glyph procurement.

Proposed MAP language (draft):
- "Onramp protections: During the evaluation and the first 60 days post-go-live, Redwood will apply a surge rate for transient traffic spikes up to X tokens/day. Any sustained usage above the committed baseline for a contiguous 24-hour period will automatically switch to the staged overage slab until usage returns below the baseline for 48 consecutive hours. Glyph will not be billed above the agreed monthly overage cap of $Y without written approval from procurement."

I've attached our public rate card and a simple MAP workbook with milestone columns for staging/pilot/production and acceptance criteria. Please review and highlight any redlines.

Next steps I propose:
1) You mark acceptance or changes on the MAP_Glyph_v1.xlsx (I included target dates).
2) We slot a 30-minute call with procurement/legal this week to lock the cap number (we can suggest a neutral X tokens/day and $Y monthly cap based on your baseline).
3) Pending legal sign-off, we issue a short SOW that references the MAP and the surge protections.

Ben is copied for ops-level confirmation — Laura will coordinate contract intake.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_RateCard_Q3_v2.pdf; MAP_Glyph_v1.xlsx

Adding a quick ops note from the runtime side:

Samir — two practical knobs we typically recommend to include in the MAP to avoid surprise charges while keeping test fidelity:

- Notification threshold: set an automated email/sms at 75% of burst-cap so both teams are alerted before billed overage.
- Soft throttle during synthetic tests: we can enable a temporary request queueing policy that limits concurrent generation per API key for a pre-agreed 4-hour window (used during stress tests). This prevents runaway parallelism from amplifying token volume.
- Emergency override: allow an ops-approved, single-use surge override for one business-critical incident per quarter that bypasses the cap but requires post-incident review.

If you want, we can bake these into the MAP spreadsheet as checkboxes and include suggested default values (75% notify, 48-hour sliding window for slab revert, one override per quarter).

I'll also flag that staged-slab pricing becomes materially cheaper than flat surge for multi-day elevated usage — we can model a forecast if you share baseline qps/token/day.

Ben Carter
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

2) Please include the soft-throttle and the emergency override language in the SOW appendix so legal can see the operational controls tied to the billing safeguards.

If you send a revised MAP workbook with suggested defaults and a redlined SOW appendix, procurement will route to legal. We can do the 30-minute call after legal has the concrete numbers to discuss.
